response.rationale: R2 is champion because two independent AFB PCR probes, from the hilar lymph node and repeat sinus FESS, are positive and provide definitive mycobacterial evidence. R4 is the closest differential via noncaseating granulomas and mediastinal lymphadenopathy, but it cannot explain the positive AFB PCR and is further weakened by normal ACE. R3 fits the nasal destruction but is contradicted by normal ANCA and the positive AFB PCR. R1 is nonspecific, and C1 is an overly narrow completion of R2 that omits the sinus PCR positivity.

rejected.why: Noncaseating granulomas and mediastinal lymphadenopathy mimic sarcoidosis, but positive AFB PCR in two specimens and normal ACE make sarcoidosis untenable.
Nasal destruction and crusting fit GPA, but ANCA is normal and positive AFB PCR indicates infection rather than autoimmune vasculitis.
Chronic rhinosinusitis explains crusting and recurrent sinusitis but not mediastinal lymphadenopathy, noncaseating granulomas, or positive AFB PCR.
Append-only completion narrowing to hilar lymph node tuberculosis ignores the second positive FESS AFB PCR and sinonasal disease; R2 is the more complete tuberculosis diagnosis.
